content: Puffing is a method used to draw smoke, typically from tobacco, into the oral cavity. This process involves creating negative pressure, which allows the smoke to come into contact with the mucous membranes and taste receptors in the mouth. Through this interaction, nicotine is absorbed, and the flavors present in the tar particles can be detected. The effect of puffing is transient, lasting only a few seconds at most, after which the smoke is exhaled. When smoking cigars or pipes, individuals typically take a puff every few minutes, depending on personal preference, although some smokers may choose to do so less frequently. Unlike cigarette smoking, the smoke is generally not inhaled directly into the lungs during puffing. The primary focus of puffing is on the taste experience, which is why many types of tobacco are manufactured with added flavors and aromas, such as vanilla, to enhance the sensory appeal.
